explanation: The dataset is small with 90 rows, 4 numeric features, and balanced three-class counts, so a moderate CatBoost configuration is a safer first real model than deeper or longer-boosted variants. This experiment directly addresses the observed evidence by replacing the chance-level dummy baseline with a regularized tree ensemble. A switch to another family would only be justified after repeated real-model failures, which have not occurred yet.
diagnosis: Only a dummy baseline has been evaluated; it scored 0.3333 accuracy, matching chance for three balanced classes. No real tabular model has yet been tested, so there is no evidence of repeated model failures and no reason to infer overfitting or underfitting from prior model trials.
next_action: Train and validate a moderate CatBoost classifier with 600 iterations, depth 6, learning rate 0.05, and l2_leaf_reg 3, then compare its validation accuracy against the 0.3333 dummy baseline.
abandoned_strategy: The dummy/constant baseline strategy is abandoned because it only reaches chance-level accuracy and provides no predictive signal beyond the class distribution.
